title: Retry-safe vCenter virtual machine provisioning
prompt: Make virtual machine provisioning retry-safe in `src/VcenterVmProvisioner.java`. The client is a dependency-free, single-file Java integration for the vSphere Automation API of a VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 vCenter. Before implementing, research `Vcenter.VM_list` and `Vcenter.VM_create` in `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` from VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`. Confirm their `/api` base path, methods, paths, authentication, form-exploded filters, request and response schemas, status codes, error envelopes, and required versus optional properties. Cite the exact specification URLs you consulted in your final answer. Use only those two operations. ensureVirtualMachine currently issues the create unconditionally, so running the same provisioning step twice leaves two virtual machines of the same name behind. Rework it so that repeating the call with the same request leaves exactly one virtual machine in the target folder: look the machine up by name within its folder before creating it, skip the create when it is already there, and when the create answers HTTP 400 with error_type ALREADY_EXISTS, adopt the machine the concurrent caller already produced rather than failing or creating again. Outcome.created() must report true only for the call that actually created the machine. Two wire details have to be corrected along the way. The list filters use OpenAPI form serialization with explode true, so every filter value travels as its own repeated query parameter instead of one delimiter-joined value. And every property of Vcenter.VM.CreateSpec except guest_os is optional: a property the caller never set must be left out of the request document entirely rather than sent as null, as an empty object, or as an empty array, and that holds at every depth, placement, cpu, memory, disks[].new_vmdk and nics[].backing included. Preserve the public API and the spec-derived property names; the constructor, ensureVirtualMachine, createVirtualMachine, listVirtualMachines, Outcome, VmSummary, VmRequest and VcenterApiException are all used as they stand, and the client must remain a single Java source file. Change only `src/VcenterVmProvisioner.java`. Run `python3 tests/verify.py`.
